stem:
Riya is helping her mother in the kitchen. She presses a ball of dough with her hands, and later she pushes a rolling pin that was lying still on the shelf, making it roll across the table.
Which statement about the effect of an applied force is correct?

options.text: A force only counts when it makes an object start moving from rest.
An applied force can change an object's shape as well as its state of motion.
A force changes the direction of an object first, and that change then produces the applied force.
An applied force can change the speed of an object but can never change its shape.

teacher.key_rationale: Pressing the dough changes its shape and pushing the rolling pin changes its state of motion, so B correctly states both effects of an applied force. A wrongly restricts force to motion from rest, C reverses the cause-effect relationship, and D omits the shape-change effect.
